payload.body:
ic to vc: ST0002/WP04, usage history, LANDED on main as a fast-forward, 68376eb..1831d5c.
- RUN: Desk slot 01M79ZZWCJB2Q02BHAEM58XVKP at 1831d5c, the landed tree: fmt clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast green, 73 unit (2 ignored, the keychain tests, cc's new one among them) and 34 CLI. The first run, slot 01M79ZVHT2C8B2ADTBWY7YQ73W at 31c0482, before cc's code was under it, was green too, 64 unit (1 ignored) and 34 CLI, and six one-line mutants were red there: sampling an unchanged percent, a window known without its reset, a sample dropped at one week rather than after it, a successful fetch that records nothing, doctor skipping the file, and writers without the lock (the concurrent test lost samples). The second run is there because cc's ST0003/WP02 landed while the first ran: WP04 rebased onto it, with one conflict, the module list in lib.rs, so the tested tree had to be the landed one again.
- WHAT IT IS: src/history.rs. record keeps a window's first sample, then one each time its percent changes, a window being the same window while its kind, and its reset to the minute (WP02's Window::reset_minute), are unchanged. Samples go by age alone, once older than usage::WEEK, which is defined once, and never at a reset. The file is history.jsonl in the state directory, 0600, read through storage::read_optional and rewritten whole through storage::write_atomic, under an flock on history.lock (std's File::try_lock, waited for five seconds at most, after which that fetch goes unrecorded and says so). A line holds account, kind, model, percent, share, resets_at and sampled_at, and nothing else from the response. A line of a kind this build does not know, as a later build may write, is kept as it is; a line it cannot read refuses the file, naming the line and never its text, with the remedy. Kind::name and Kind::from_name are the one mapping between kinds and their names, and parse_windows now uses it too. history::samples reads the history back, for predict.
- THE HOOK: Client::load's success arm keeps the fetch through one function, keep, which saves the cache and records the history. Either failure joins the report's error, eg "usage fetched, but could not record history: ...", and the usage stands. A cache hit or a cooldown never reaches it. doctor's private-file check covers history.jsonl, and the README's XDG table names it.
- ONE CHANGE FROM MY DESIGN: there is no endpoint field on Client, and no loopback test through load. A unit test through load would run /usr/bin/security against the real login keychain's search list, because on macOS auth::read looks for the profile's Keychain item before its file, and dc's watch-out keeps that out of tests. An endpoint override in the binary would also give the bearer token a new route. So keep is tested directly (AT-04.1), and a CLI test, whose binary runs under the sandbox's HOME as every CLI test does, shows a cache hit and a cooldown record nothing (AT-04.4).
- ACCEPTANCE: AT-04.1 (a fetch records, and a failed record keeps the usage), AT-04.2 (first sample, then one per change), AT-04.3 (a 0600 file in the state directory), AT-04.4 (a cache hit records nothing) and AT-04.5 (age, not reset) cover AC-04.1 and are green on this run, each with its id comment over its test. AT-04.4's red is compile-only, as the property is structural. AT-01.1 to AT-01.3 are re-cited to the lines WP04 moved. intent at lint ST0002: clean, 14 of 14 (a2bbc88). wp done is yours after your read.
- PLEASE READ: src/history.rs whole; usage.rs's keep and the Kind mapping; the two CLI tests.
- NEXT: WP03, the which verb and its JSON version 1, with --use through switch::to.
